title: The Path of the Conquistadores: Trinidad and Venezuelan Guiana

waivers.why: p0025 is a second shot of printed p. 1 (the same as p0027); not drafted
p0026 is a blank frame between the two shots of p. 1

summary: Lindon Bates, Jr. (1883–1915), an American engineer and writer, went in 1911 by steamer from New York to Trinidad and crossed the Gulf of Paria to Venezuela. He describes Port of Spain, San Fernando, the oil region, and the Pitch Lake; the voyage by launch through the Serpent’s Mouth and up the Orinoco; Ciudad Bolívar during the centenary of Venezuelan independence; a ride on the llanos; and the return down the river on the steamer “Delta”. Most of the book is written in the present tense and addresses the reader as “you”. The first chapter is a history of Columbus, Raleigh, and the Spanish seekers of El Dorado on the same coast, with long quotations from older writers. The year of the journey is inferred from the centenary.
notes_on_text: Transcribed from the copy at the Boston Public Library (Internet Archive: pathofconquistad00bate_0). The first page of Chapter I was photographed twice; the second shot is used.
The plates and the map are printed sideways in the book and are shown upright. The book’s title, printed again above Chapter I, is left out there.
